coverage.category: 28. Notaries, land agents, real estate brokers and other professionals with periodic or anti-money-laundering reports
coverage.found: AML Law obligors include real-estate brokers and notaries (when working on property deals). Reports of cash transactions of EUR 15,000 or more and of suspicious transactions go to the Administration for the Prevention of Money Laundering. Dec 2024 amendments ban cash payments of EUR 10,000 or more. A 2024 national risk assessment flags real estate and brokerage. A proposal to amend the Law on Brokerage in Real Estate Sales and Lease was found but its content was not read.

coverage.category: 29. Hotels, guest houses and short-term rentals: guest registers, tourism levies
coverage.found: eTurista (free state central system) is mandatory for all accommodation, including uncategorised objects, from Oct 2020 per biznis.rs. Local governments register and categorise household accommodation. Flat-rate tourist tax per bed per year, set in 2019: 1,000 to 3,300 RSD; fines for unregistered letting 150,000-350,000 RSD. The Ministry (2025) demands registration numbers on platform listings; its dispute with Booking was unresolved. No new 2026 Serbian rule found.

coverage.category: 30. Small exporters and importers facing traceability or certification rules: food, fish, timber, forest-risk commodities
coverage.found: Only an old Serbian decree on a register of fruit and vegetable exporters to Russia (cold store of at least 500 t fruit or 200 t vegetables, 15-day change notices; date and status unclear). Nothing on eFito, EUDR or CBAM beyond K03. Not enough found.

coverage.found: The Serbian rules (via a search snippet, not an official page) say growers with more than 10 ari must enter the vineyard register, and the annual production declaration is due by 31 Dec. The minpolj.gov.rs page returned 503, so forms and portal are unverified.

coverage.found: The 2009 Law on Packaging and Packaging Waste and a register-keeping rulebook were found. No data on current thresholds, small-firm exemptions, annual reports or 2026 changes.

coverage.found: Law on e-Bolovanje-poslodavac applies from 1 Jan 2026; from 1 Apr 2026 employers can file wage-compensation claims electronically. Nothing new beyond K02 and K07.

candidates.name: Excise refund (refakcija) claim pack for small carriers, taxi operators and businesses heating premises
candidates.trigger: Pravilnik on excise refund, new forms REF-T (quarterly, filed at least 20 days after quarter-end) and REF-G (monthly) from 1 Oct 2025. Old-form claims are rejected. Claims go only through the Tax Administration portal for legal entities and carriers. The Tax Administration registers the claimant on the first claim and decides within 30 days. Refunds are capped at 5% above the prior-year average consumption unless justified. Needs fiscal receipts or invoices showing excise and buyer data, consumption reports, licences and vehicle documents. Transport refund rate reportedly rose to 34.56 din/l from 1 Jul 2025 (unverified).

coverage.category: 13. Small water systems
coverage.found: Thin Serbian sourcing. Rural waterworks (seoski vodovodi) are lightly controlled: about 1,263 are described as 'under some or no control', Batut found E. coli in 33% of samples from small waterworks and wells, and about 30% of rural systems need priority repair (agronews.rs, kurir.rs, slobodnaevropa.org via search snippets). Ownership of many rural systems is unresolved, so there is no clear buyer. The drinking-water rulebook (Sl. glasnik RS 28/2019) defines public supply as more than 5 households or 20 residents. No Serbian law on water for human consumption or EU 2020/2184 transposition with a deadline was found. Sampling goes to public-health institutes and is paid through public tenders. Low willingness to pay and no clear legal duty on a defined small operator, so only a weak candidate. Unchecked: who legally operates rural systems (municipal utility, local community, citizen association) and the current Law on Waters and Law on Communal Activities provisions.

coverage.category: 33. Retail fiscalisation and e-fiscalisation changes (small shops, caterers)
coverage.found: E-fiscalisation has applied since 2022. Market-stall vendors are exempt only until 31 Dec 2026 (Decree on activities without the duty to record retail sales through a fiscal device, amended Dec 2025; biznis.rs 8 Dec 2025). The next step is unclear: the article said it 'remains to be seen' whether this is a new model or an obligation from 2027. Amendments to the Law on Fiscalisation (Sl. glasnik RS 80/2026, in force 8 Sep 2026) extend the one-year ban on trading to cases where the QR code on a receipt was not generated by the Tax Administration's system or points to an unrelated receipt, with immediate imposition, including at event venues (KPMG Serbia). Fiscal-device and POS vendors, plus the state subsidy for devices, already cover the core job. Candidate: a market-stall switchover pack. Unchecked: the post-2026 model for stalls, and the vendor field for stall-sized fiscal devices.

coverage.category: 34. Excise goods traders (tobacco, alcohol, fuel excise warehouses)
coverage.found: The e-akciza system (Law on Excise as amended, Uredba of 28 Sep 2024) puts requests for control stamps and excise-warehouse permits online, and obliged persons record used, unused and damaged stamps so that quarterly reports to the Ministry of Finance are auto-filled (pravniportal.com). Excise returns are filed twice a month from 1 Jan 2026. Tobacco and non-combustible tobacco are to be tracked through the whole chain by aggregate GS1 codes scanned at dispatch and receipt (not at retail intake). Excise on e-cigarette liquids and CNG is new. E-otpremnice for excise-goods movement apply from 1 Jan 2026 and for all private trade from 1 Oct 2027; this is covered by K01, K09 and K10. Fuel excise refund (refakcija): new REF-T and REF-G forms from 1 Oct 2025, claimed on the Tax Administration portal; see the candidates. Tobacco wholesalers and retailers keep records under a Uprava za duvan rulebook; contents and any annual report not confirmed. Fuel excise warehouse operators and small fuel distributors were not covered by any source found. Unchecked: the excise-warehouse permit rules for fuel and the vendor field for tobacco chain scanning.

result.competitor: No lift-specific inspection or maintenance tracker for the Serbian market was found. Partial overlap from general building-management apps for upravnici: Troškovi.com (web app for upravnici with an obligations calendar, notices, minutes, multi-building), InfoZgrada (iOS app for fault reporting and assemblies), and Stanko/mojstanko.com (MND Labs: fault reporting, document archive, multi-building). JP Gradsko stambeno services about 6,500 Belgrade lifts monthly as part of a bundled service. Lift service firms (100+, unregistered) handle the servicing themselves. Generic international lift maintenance software (e.g. Joblogic) exists but nothing localised was found.
result.duty: Pravilnik o pregledima liftova u upotrebi, Sl. glasnik RS 105/2024, published 26.12.2024 and in force from 3.1.2025 (replaces the 2017 rulebook). Art. 5 (per the Belgrade Chamber of Commerce lift council, quoted by biznis.rs): the lift owner must ensure regular and extraordinary inspections by a designated body (imenovano telo), safe use, maintenance and rescue; in residential buildings the owner is the stambena zajednica. The Uredba o održavanju stambenih zgrada lists regular lift servicing as current maintenance (tekuće održavanje). Not confirmed: the regular inspection interval (the PDF text could not be extracted; the 'yearly' claim comes from a 2002 Vreme article) and the penalty amounts (none found). The April 2026 'Pravilnik o projektovanju, izradi i održavanju liftova' was only a working draft (15-day public comment period), and I found no sign it has been adopted.
result.market: About 25,000 lifts in residential buildings in Serbia, half of them in Belgrade, and about 15,000 overdue for replacement (Belgrade Chamber of Commerce figure via Kurir, Nov 2018). JP Gradsko stambeno maintains about 6,500, Vojno stambeno about 2,000, and about 3,000 owners contract private firms; about 2,000 lifts lack regular maintenance or valid certificates. There are 100+ lift service firms with no register or licence (biznis.rs, 2021). No national lift register was found.
result.reason: The duty is real, but the claim cites the wrong rulebook. The 2017 Pravilnik was replaced by Pravilnik o pregledima liftova u upotrebi (Sl. glasnik RS 105/2024), in force since 3 Jan 2025. The owner (in residential buildings, the housing community) must ensure regular and extraordinary inspections, maintenance and rescue. I could not confirm the inspection interval or any fine: the PDFs were unreadable, and the Vreme "yearly inspection" article dates from 2002. Enforcement looks weak. No lift-specific software was found. General building apps (Troškovi.com with an obligations calendar, InfoZgrada, Stanko) partly cover reminders. The task is tracking one inspection date per building, which is low pain. Lift service firms do the visits themselves, so housing communities would likely pay little.

result.reason: Duty is real: the 2021 Law on Items of Precious Metals requires registered buyers (APR plus DMDM register) to buy only at a marked buying point, issue an otkupni list per purchase (fineness, price) and keep a purchase record. Fines are up to 2M RSD for companies and 50k-500k RSD for sole traders. Market inspection supervises. Not checked: whether a current amended text exists, and the number of registered buyers (no register count found). Two searches found no dedicated software, but this is weak evidence. No periodic report to an authority was found. The duty is per-transaction paperwork, not a filing, and the buyer group is small. A paper form or generic POS likely suffices. Low willingness to pay.

The draft Law on Passenger Transport in Road Traffic was in consultation until 2 Sep 2026. No source I found shows it adopted, and no entry-into-force date is known. The platform duty to verify the carrier's approval and the driver's taxi licence appears only in the draft. Current law does require taxi approvals and driver licences, issued by city or municipal administrations, but the draft's new duties are not in force. Competition: Yandex Go already works only with licensed associations. I did not find a dedicated compliance tool. I did not search for dispatch software. The duty falls mostly on platforms and associations, so the buyer base is small and mainly large. Market size was not found. Score stays low at 3.

Duty is real but not yet in force. Market vendors selling non-own goods are exempt from e-fiscal recording until 31 Dec 2026 (Tax Administration notice, Dec 2025). It has been postponed repeatedly (2022, 2024, 2025, 2026). A July 2026 Novosti piece still gives 31 Dec 2026 and doesn't confirm a 2027 start. Biznis.rs says it is unclear whether it will start in 2027. I found no market-specific app or software product, but searches were limited. Fiscal devices and POS hardware are the likely competitors, and I didn't check them. Vendor count wasn't found. Buyers are low-margin, protest-prone, and pay a flat tax. The recurring workflow doesn't exist yet and may slip again. This is a one-off, hardware-heavy and politically uncertain opportunity.

The duty looks real but is only partly confirmed. Search snippets say guards must file for relicensing at the police administration of their residence, at the earliest 60 days before the 5-year licence expires. They also say the licence is issued on personal request. I could not open the law or the amendment (the PDF fetch returned 403), so I can't confirm the current text, fees or penalties. The amendment's adoption is unconfirmed. The 45,000 licence figure is old, and I found no current count. The core job is a date reminder, since each guard files personally and the state issues the licence. No dedicated competitor turned up, but my Serbian search was thin and general HR or Excel tools cover it. Buyers are many tiny agencies and individual guards, so willingness to pay is low. The 2021-22 renewal peak has passed.

result.reason: Serbia has a real duty: growers with at least 0.1 ha (10 ari) who sell grapes must register in the Vineyard Register, and wine producers must register in the Winery Register. Registration can be done at any time. A FAOLEX legal text (via search summary only, not opened) gives an annual production declaration by 10 November, not 31 December, so the claim's trigger looks wrong (the 31 Dec date is Croatian). No penalty found. Registration is tied to subsidies, so it is a one-off entry, not a recurring workflow. A new Wine Law is only a draft (consultation ended 6 June 2026, applies from August 2027) and plans a central e-register. No competitor or e-service found, but the official page returned 503. Market size not found. Weak recurring pain, so a low score.

The duty is real. The Law on Packaging and Packaging Waste (Sl. glasnik 36/2009, amended 95/2018) and its Rulebook on report forms require producers, importers and packers to file an annual report with the Environmental Protection Agency (SEPA) by 31 March. SEPA passes it to the Fund by 30 April, and the Fund issues a fee decision. Obligors can instead sign with one of 8 licensed operators (Sekopak and others), who then handle the reporting. In 2021 there were 1,924 firms in operator systems and 247 outside. I found no penalty amounts, no small-firm exemption and no software competitor, but did not check them directly. The market is small and funnels through operators. Low willingness to pay, reporting is a form, and PPWR export compliance is only a side angle. The 2026 status of the law is unconfirmed.

Registered precious-metal buyers have a mandatory purchase-record duty; small firms in scope.
Small taxi and minibus operators face licence and driver-approval duties under a new law.
Market-stall vendors face a fiscalisation deadline; one-off duty hitting many small firms.
End-of-life vehicle dismantlers are a different buyer group and duty (certificate of destruction) from K06 waste-movement documents; related K06.
Small associations and co-operatives have a beneficial-owner filing duty; in scope, needs verification.
Private kindergartens have a mandatory enrolment register and reporting duty; small licensed premises.
Small septic haulers face local licensing and contract duties; weak but unchecked, so keep.
Small dealers and applicators may face spraying-record duties; unverified, so keep.
Funeral firms and cemetery operators are small businesses facing a planned law; unverified, so keep.
